lines: The room is cold. The bed is warm.
This is where it is decided.
They look like two words. They are one.
Both grow from a single Latin root: discere. To learn.
Discipline is what a learner does, again and again, until the learning is true.
Walk across a field once, and the grass stands back up.
Walk it twice, and the grass remembers.
A week. A faint line, if you know where to look.
A month. Now anyone could see it.
A hundred days. You could not miss it now.
A path is not made by wanting to arrive.
It is only what is left, when a walk is repeated.
Some mornings you will want it.
Most mornings you will feel nothing.
Some mornings you will want to quit.
Two thousand years ago, a Roman poet wrote:
not by force, but by falling often.
The water is no stronger than the rock.
Nothing dramatic ever happens. A drop. Another drop.
You will hear a voice, with excellent reasons.
Five more minutes. You were tired yesterday.
The voice is not your enemy. It is only tired.
Do not debate it. Not at five in the morning.
The first step is not the work.
The first step is to stop negotiating.
Put your feet on the floor.
The grass will start to cover the path,
and a voice will say: it is over.
A path is not erased in a day.
The grass is slower than your doubt.
It is the habit of coming back.
Nobody thanks you in the rain.
The path does not care how you feel.
It only asks one question: are you here?
Through every season, the same walk.
Discipline is a kind of love:
the kind that keeps showing up, after the feeling has gone.
And one day, you stop, and look back.
Someone is walking where you walked.
They do not know your name.
They only know the way is clear.
That is what a disciple is: someone who learns by following.
And a teacher is only a disciple who did not stop.
Small enough to do on your worst day.
Tell me your one thing in the comments.
Thank you for spending your time here.
